pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Individual dark regions are organized into irregular polygons with distinct angular vertices. The edges exhibit sharp pixel gradients transitioning to the light-colored corridor network. Relative spatial area of patches is heterogeneous, with smaller units clustered towards the lower-left boundary of the subject.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: The interstitial network forms a continuous lattice of light-colored pathways. Junction nodes exhibit primarily tri-radial connectivity. Pixel thickness is consistent throughout the visible field, providing a uniform separation between the primary patch structures.

other_distinctive_markers: The internal area of the dark patches contains secondary, higher-density pigmentation clusters (stippling) that are non-uniformly distributed across the surface.
